newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mostly higher before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mostly higher before FOMC.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly higher but trading was thin ahead of Tuesday's U.S. FOMC.

The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Tuesday to consider whether to raise U.S. interest rates. Analysts remain divided, though the latest Reuters survey showed a slight bias toward a 25-basis-point increase. With expectations for a 25-basis-point rate rise already factored into the dollar, currency futures drifted higher during the light session.
The Jewish Yom Kippur religious holiday and a Japanese holiday kept the trading pits thin.

December Swiss francs drifted to the highest price in a week, benefitting from the currency's safe-haven status amid concerns about President Boris Yeltsin's health. Reports that Yeltsin suffered a third heart attack earlier this year and that his planned open heart surgery had been postponed kept pressure on mark/Swiss, traders said.
Still, December marks were well supported and climbed to minor gains in a recovery from overnight selling.
Marks overnight were hit by talk that a meeting in Dublin of European central bankers and finance ministers was upbeat about the drive to a European Monetary Union starting in 1999.
Mark futures recovered in Chicago trading and December closed up $0.0015 at $0.6651.
Overall trading in the futures pits was quiet because of the holidays, with contracts posting very tight ranges. Technicians said Monday's action was merely a pause in the market.
"It was liking watching planks warp," an IMM trader said of the quiet day. Traders called flows light and featureless.
Still, speculation abounded about how the dollar would react to a possible Fed rate hike on Tuesday.

"I think 25 basis points would be good for the dollar," an IMM trader said. He said the dollar could sell off briefly if the Fed stands pat and said a 50-basis-point rate hike would launch the dollar to 1.5205 marks and 111.05 yen. He cited as good dollar support perceptions that a tightening cycle was at hand.

Dec yen ended up $0.000004 to $0.009209, marks gained $0.0015 to $0.6651, Swiss francs rose $0.0024 to $0.8165, pound rose $0.0010 at $1.5556, Can dollar was up $0.0001 at $0.7343, Aussie dollar was up $0.0003 at $0.7902, Mexican peso rose $0.000225 to $0.125750.
